literal: Than living a life of backbiting and lying, dying will, even by the decree of virtue, give benefit.
translation: Dying is far better than living a life of deceit and backbiting; even the god of death will deem such a death as a virtue that brings benefit.
modern: புறம்பேசிப் பொய் சொல்லி உயிர் வாழ்வதை விடச் சாதல் சிறந்தது; அது அறநெறிப்படியும் நன்மையைத் தரும்.
explanation: This couplet emphasizes the extreme dishonor of backbiting and deceitful living. The author states that it is much better to die than to sustain one's life through slander and lies. Even the god of death, who acts as the arbiter of virtue, will consider such a death as a beneficial and righteous choice rather than a sinful life. The key words 'புறங்கூறி' (backbiting) and 'பொய்த்து' (lying) represent the vices, while 'சாதல்' (dying) is presented as a superior alternative that brings 'ஆக்கம்' (benefit/goodness).
